In today's world, people use two different calendars: the western calendar and the Lunar calendar.
The western calendar is solar. It follows the sun. The Lunar calendar follows the moon and the sun, but the moon is more important.
It takes the Earth about 365 days to go around the sun, so the calendar has 365 days. Every four years, there is a leap year with 366 days.
The ancient Romans made it about 2,000 years ago. July is named after Julius Caesar, an important Roman leader. Korea started to use it in 1896.
The moon goes around the Earth about every 29 and a half days. There are usually 12 months in a year, and an extra month comes every two or three years.
Each year is named after an animal, in a 12-year cycle. Most Korean holidays still follow this calendar.
The western calendar follows the moon.
